questions.title: Implement a custom Debounce function in JavaScript.
questions.description:
Custom Debounce Function

Debouncing limits the rate at which a function gets triggered. It ensures that a function is called only after a certain amount of time has elapsed since it was last invoked.

Common use-cases: Window resizing, typing in search bars, scroll-based calculations.
questions.bestPractices:
• Ensure the debounced function retains the lexical scope (this) and arguments of the original invocation.
  • Implement a cancel() method to clear pending timers.
questions.commonMistakes: • Losing context (this) when calling the debounced function inside event listeners.
questions.example:
function debounce(fn, delay) {
  let timeoutId = null;
  
  const debounced = function(...args) {
    const context = this;
    
    if (timeoutId) {
      clearTimeout(timeoutId);
    }
    
    timeoutId = setTimeout(() => {
      fn.apply(context, args);
    }, delay);
  };
  
  debounced.cancel = function() {
    if (timeoutId) {
      clearTimeout(timeoutId);
      timeoutId = null;
    }
  };
  
  return debounced;
}
questions.interviewTip: Make sure you include `this` and arguments propagation using closure. This shows your depth of closures, lexical scopes, and function application.

questions.title: Implement a custom Throttle function in JavaScript.
questions.description:
Custom Throttle Function

Throttling guarantees that a function executes at most once in every specified duration. Useful for scroll events, drag-and-drop actions, or mouse movements.
questions.bestPractices:
• Make sure arguments and contexts are correctly preserved.
  • Ensure the trailing edge execution fires if a call happens during the cooldown window.
questions.commonMistakes: • Forgetting to execute the final call that happened during the wait period (trailing edge), which can leave layout positions outdated.
questions.example:
function throttle(fn, limit) {
  let lastFunc;
  let lastRan;
  return function(...args) {
    const context = this;
    if (!lastRan) {
      fn.apply(context, args);
      lastRan = Date.now();
    } else {
      clearTimeout(lastFunc);
      lastFunc = setTimeout(function() {
        if ((Date.now() - lastRan) >= limit) {
          fn.apply(context, args);
          lastRan = Date.now();
        }
      }, limit - (Date.now() - lastRan));
    }
  }
}
questions.interviewTip: Describe the differences: debounce delays execution until quiet, whereas throttle periodically runs execution at a fixed interval during continuous events.
